I saved the Snake game as one self-contained file: `snake_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html`. I haven't opened it in a browser or played it, so nothing below has been tested yet.

It was built to cover everything you asked for:
- **Board and movement:** a 30×30 grid where the snake moves on its own in one of four directions and grows when it eats food. Hitting a wall, itself or the other snake ends the game.
- **Game modes:** a start menu lets you pick human vs human, CPU vs human or CPU vs CPU.
- **Controls:** player 1 uses WASD and player 2 uses the arrow keys.
- **CPU snake:** it looks for a path to the food and tries to steer clear of collisions.
- **Score:** each snake's score is shown while you play.
- **Game over:** a game over screen shows the result. Press a key to restart the same mode or go back to the menu.

To play, open the file in any browser.

Two snakes: Player 1 (green, WASD) and Player 2 (blue, Arrow keys). Snakes move continuously on a fixed tick (~100ms) with input queue preventing 180-degree reversal. Food: a single food item randomly placed on empty cell; eating grows snake by 1 and +1 score (respawn food). Game ends when any snake dies; game over screen shows winner (or draw) and both scores, \"Press Space/Enter to restart, M or Esc for menu\". Restart replays the same mode. CPU AI: BFS from head to food avoiding walls and all snake bodies (tail cells that will move treated as free); if no path, choose safe move maximizing reachable area via flood fill; avoid cells adjacent to opponent head when possible. Score HUD above canvas showing P1 and P2 scores with labels (Human/CPU) and current mode. Clean dark styling, centered layout, grid lines subtle, snake heads drawn with eyes or darker shade. Pause with P optional."}
